change: Construct the complete custom-lookup pending and root snapshots in one collection instead of allocating a prefix/clone and then growing it.

contract.before: Build [unused marker], append the original call values; later clone those values and append the selected Method for rooting.
contract.after: Collect the same marker/value and value/Method sequences directly into their complete owned vectors.
preserved: The exact Oop order, owned argument snapshots and call roots.
Consumed-continuation checks and removal of references from the consumed context.
Lookup, captured Method meaning, suspension, native barriers, GC and failure behavior.
Managed continuation objects, allocations and driver steps.

microbenchmark.scope: Repeated existing prepareSend transfers in an independent C continuation. Normal lookup control and custom metacircular forwarding lookup; logical arities 0,1,8,64 plus a loop counter. Each timed sample has four 512-transfer runs; includes initial/final entry overhead. Serial ABBA, seven samples/process, GC outside timing; every argument and result checked.

validation: Independent C continuation suite including custom/metacircular lookup, pause/replacement, entered roots, late replies, GC and allocation accounting.
Full Oop core/compiler/GC and negative dispatch/construction contracts.
rejected_scope: Pre-sizing ordinary entry vectors showed mixed results, including zero-argument regressions. Those edits were reverted. Only the two always-appending custom-lookup snapshots remain changed.
limits: About 3.5% lower CPU in the custom-lookup transfer benchmark; ordinary-lookup control is effectively unchanged. No general language speedup claimed.
Initial control timings were noisy, so alternating fresh-process runs were extended before retaining the change.
Automatic GC disabled only for timed diagnostic work; precise collection occurs between samples. Runtime policy is unchanged.
No installed user runtime was replaced.
